historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly requires a reachable GPIO controller and post-boot evidence, but exposes credentials, disables host identity checking and conflates controller-side power-on with host-side uptime in one SSH session.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly prevents invocation against an already-on SUT and requires OOB observation, yet does not correct the transport contradiction introduced by its host-SSH command.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Rows146-148 form distinct immediate-off, state-read and standby-to-on GPIO coverage. This row must preserve the power-on transition and cannot be satisfied by only querying status or normal OS reboot.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Execute `power_on` only from the approved always-on BMC/service-controller domain, independently observe standby-to-on rails and boot stages, then establish a separate secure host session for OS health.

original_test_intent: Verify that the platform GPIO power controller can transition a host from the defined standby state to on and that the host completes a normal boot with expected system health.
original_method: Identify the exact always-on controller, script version and `power_on` semantics; confirm AC present, standby rails stable and host actually off without active workloads; obtain approval for one transition; from secure BMC/UART/controller access invoke the literal source command once; independently timestamp rail/chassis power and boot-stage changes; after OS network readiness, open a separate verified host session to collect uptime and complete health/log checks; stop without automatic retry on any ambiguous state or boot failure.
manual_activity: The owner confirms standby, maintenance window and recovery; an operator maintains BMC/UART/OOB observation and authorizes the single transition. The agent may invoke the approved controller-side command and later collect host health only after confirmation.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC identity and authoritative always-on location, version/hash/owner of `/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh`
Exact `power_on` GPIO/rail target, pulse/level behavior, idempotence and expected command response
Authoritative standby definition including AC, standby rails, host/chassis state and no-active-workload evidence
Secure BMC/controller access and independent UART/rail/chassis power observer
Power-on, rail-good, POST and OS-network/service timeout sequence with abort criteria
Owner-approved recovery path and post-boot firmware/device/filesystem/service/log health oracle
safety_requirements: Do not invoke `power_on` until target identity and stable standby/off state are independently confirmed
Run the transition from the documented always-on controller, not through an impossible host-OS SSH session
Use secure injected credentials and verified controller/host identity; reject `sshpass -p` and disabled host-key checking
Capture one command and independent rail/chassis/UART transition timeline with bounded timeouts
Stop if already on, standby is inconsistent, power rails sequence incorrectly, POST stalls, devices disappear or critical logs appear
Do not issue another power-on, power-cycle or reset automatically; use the separately approved recovery path
agent_execution_scope: Validate controller script identity/semantics and securely collect pre-state evidence
After approval, issue one exact controller-side `power_on` and capture stdout/stderr/exit/timestamps
Correlate independent power/boot evidence and, only after host readiness, collect secure OS uptime and health
Do not guess script domain/GPIO semantics, expose credentials, invoke against an on/unknown host, retry automatically or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve script execution domain, version/hash and exact GPIO/rail power-on behavior
Approve standby definition, maintenance window, observer, timing and single-transition/no-retry policy
Review transition plus post-boot evidence and issue the DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The source `power_on` and later status/uptime evidence are relevant, but a single host-SSH command cannot begin while the host is in standby and cannot survive its own power-on/boot transition. The insecure password and host-key options are also unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: From secure always-on BMC/controller access, run only `/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh power_on` once after standby approval; observe status/rails/UART independently, then create a new secure host session after network readiness for uptime and health checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC UART context, standby precondition, exact `power_on` path, power-status-on and normal-operation checks, Common branch and 15/15-minute estimate are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform one controller-side standby-to-on GPIO transition with independent rail/UART timing, then verify OS health through a separate post-boot session.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds execution-domain proof, exact standby/GPIO semantics, secure access, independent transition timing, staged controller-versus-host sessions and explicit recovery/no-retry boundaries.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A script exit, immediate five-second delay or later uptime alone does not prove a correct GPIO transition, rail sequence, POST path or absence of degraded devices.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Issuing power-on in an already-on or indeterminate state can trigger vendor-specific pulse/reset behavior or mask a failed rail/boot sequence.

project_override_considerations: The project must provide the always-on controller transport. A host SSH wrapper may be used only for post-boot health, never as an implicit substitute for the controller-side source command.
expected_evidence: SUT/BMC/controller identity, script path/version/hash/owner and exact GPIO/power-on semantics
Pre-action AC/standby-rail/chassis-off state, idle/no-workload proof and approval timestamp
Secure controller session and exact `power_on` stdout/stderr/exit/timestamp
Independent rail/chassis/BMC/UART transition timeline through POST and OS readiness with timeouts
Separate secure host session showing boot ID/uptime, expected devices/services/filesystems and power status
BMC SEL plus OS boot/kernel/service logs, recovery actions if any and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently describes one standby-to-on GPIO transition followed by normal operation. The exact script domain and standby oracle are underspecified project inputs; the infeasible SSH wrapper belongs to historical reviews, not the Master source.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The controller-side source method is identifiable and executable once script location, standby definition, approval and recovery are supplied, so the case remains RPUC rather than BLOCKED.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row148 Wistron-HW Robust-00465-V002: identify the always-on BMC/service-controller domain, secure transport and version/hash/owner of `/usr/bin/powerctrl.sh`; define exact `power_on` GPIO/rail target and pulse/idempotence response, authoritative AC/standby/chassis-off oracle, independent rail/UART/POST/OS timeline and timeouts; approve one transition, no-retry/recovery policy and separate post-boot host uptime/device/service/filesystem/log acceptance.

review_improvement: Preserves the literal GPIO power-on coverage while correcting the impossible host-SSH transport and separating controller transition evidence from the later host-OS health session.
independent_technical_reasoning: A host in standby cannot accept an OS SSH command, so the source's preceding BMC-UART step must be treated as evidence that `powerctrl.sh` belongs to an always-on management domain unless engineering says otherwise. Power-on success also has phases: GPIO assertion, rail-good, POST and OS readiness. Combining `power_on; sleep 5; power_status; uptime` in one host session skips the domain transition and substitutes a fixed delay for staged oracles. The valid contract uses a secure controller session for the single action and independent observation, followed by a new host session only after boot.
